title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reading.body:
This is a false match by an automated plate reader, produced at the point where a camera turns an image into an alert. The system reads letters and numbers only, so a plate number that Kansas issues more than once is treated as a single identity. The alert then reaches officers as a possible stolen vehicle, carrying the weight of a database hit without the plate type or background that would separate the two vehicles.

The checks that could have caught it sit in two places. One is the camera, which would have to read plate backgrounds, the change Wichita police have asked Flock to train. The other is the officer, since alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but an officer may still act if the wrong plate type was entered. In Colwich an officer recognised the minivan and the stop ended there. In Catoosa the stop went ahead with guns drawn and handcuffs. Kansas is moving to seven digit numbers that are not duplicated, which removes the ambiguity at the source.

What is not established is that the camera system or the officers acted unlawfully, and no finding of fault has been reported. The account rests on a single news investigation.

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were repeatedly stopped because their Kansas KU Alumni plate, number 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary tag. In Colwich, Kansas, a Flock camera alerted police to a possible stolen vehicle, but an officer recognized their minivan and learned the stolen tag had the same number on a different plate background. About a month later in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock alert led police to stop them with guns drawn and handcuffs.

Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate types or backgrounds. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty, and it duplicates numbers. Alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but if the wrong plate type was entered, officers may still act. Wichita police have spoken with Flock about training its AI to recognize plate backgrounds. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit numbers that are not duplicated. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, and they hope to keep their 14 year old plate.
